questions.model_text_raw:
Rule 23 of the Trade Marks Rules, 2017 governs the form and signing of a trademark application.  

An application for registration of a trademark in respect of a specification of goods or services must be made in Form TM‑A and must be signed by the applicant or his authorised agent [1].  

The application must (a) contain a precise description by words of the trademark where necessary to determine the applicant’s right, (b) be capable of depicting the graphical representation of the trademark, (c) be treated as a three‑dimensional trademark only if the application includes a statement to that effect, and (d) be treated as a colour‑combination trademark only if the application includes a statement to that effect [1].  

If an amendment is required to divide an application under the proviso to section 22, the amendment must be filed in Form TM‑M [1].  

A non‑series application must relate to one trademark only, although it may cover as many classes of goods or services as are desired [1].  

Where an application seeks registration of all goods or services in a class, or a large variety of goods or services in a class, the Registrar may refuse to accept the application unless he is satisfied that the specification is justified by the use (or intended use) of the trademark; the names of goods and services must, as far as possible, correspond to those in the classification published by the Registrar under sub‑rule (2) of Rule 20 [1].  

If a single application is filed and the Registrar determines that the goods or services fall in additional class(es) beyond those applied for, the applicant must either restrict the specification to the originally applied class(es) or amend the application to add the additional class(es) by filing a request on Form TM‑M and paying the appropriate fee; where all goods or services fall in a different class, the Registrar may permit correction of the class by filing the request on Form TM‑M [1].  

Thus, Rule 23 specifies that the prescribed form is TM‑A, the signature must be that of the applicant or agent, and any amendments or class corrections must use Form TM‑M, with the Registrar retaining discretion to refuse overly broad specifications.
